name: TypeScript

image.dockerfile:
FROM node:24-slim
RUN npm install -g typescript@5 && npm cache clean --force

levelNotes.3: Good topics: discriminated unions with exhaustive switch (never), readonly arrays, generic helpers.
levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: generics with constraints, mapped/conditional types in a public API, type guards, branded types.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: typed event emitters, builder APIs with accumulated generics, template literal types for parsers.

image.dockerfile:
FROM node:24-slim
WORKDIR /opt/eco
RUN npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --no-audit --no-fund typescript@5.8.3 vitest@2.1.9 fastify@5.2.1 zod@3.23.8 && npm cache clean --force && ln -s /opt/eco/node_modules/.bin/tsc /usr/local/bin/tsc

ecosystem.testCommand: ln -sfn /opt/eco/node_modules /work/node_modules && tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2022 --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --allowImportingTsExtensions --erasableSyntaxOnly ../$TARGET/*.ts && /opt/eco/node_modules/.bin/vitest run --root /work/tests --reporter verbose
ecosystem.conventions: Tests use vitest 2.1 (describe/it/expect, it.each, vi.fn, vi.spyOn, vi.useFakeTimers) in tests/*.test.{mjs,ts}; they load the code under test from ../$TARGET/ with a dynamic import, written EXACTLY like this because Vite only resolves template-string imports one level deep (bugs/<name>/ is two): `const target = new URL(`../${process.env.TARGET ?? "starter"}/solution.mjs`, import.meta.url).href; const { fn } = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ target);` (use solution.ts for TypeScript). Libraries resolve from the test run's node_modules (already set up by the test command): import them normally. zod 3.23 is available: derive static types from schemas with z.infer, and validate at the boundary. Only erasable TypeScript syntax (as in basics).

areas.name: Schemas as types with zod (z.infer, refinements, transforms)
Typed API contracts and parsing untrusted data
